overview: The project team hosted a community forum to present the feasibility study schedule and detail the six Medford High School building project alternatives currently under consideration.

items.title: Feasibility Study Schedule and Process Update
items.summary: Matt Gulino reviewed the Massachusetts School Building Authority process, noting that the Preliminary Design Program was submitted in February and the Preferred Schematic Report is due on June 25th.

items.title: Preferred Schematic Report Phase Deliverables
items.summary: Matt Rice outlined the technical and environmental analyses being prepared for the six remaining alternatives, which will include detailed floor and site plans, phasing diagrams, and total carbon assessments.

items.title: Alternative A.1: Code Upgrade and Repair
items.summary: Matt Rice presented the baseline Alternative A.1 design, a $437 million code-compliance repair option that would not meet the project's educational goals or qualify for state reimbursement.

items.title: Alternative B.1.2: Addition and Renovation
items.summary: Matt Rice explained Alternative B.1.2, an addition and renovation design that maximizes the preservation of the existing building frame but requires 56 modular classrooms during construction.

items.title: Alternative C2.2: Five-Story Addition and Renovation
items.summary: Matt Rice presented Alternative C2.2, which preserves northern athletic facilities while constructing a five-story addition stepped into the western hillside.

items.title: Alternative C3.4: Four-Story Addition and Renovation
items.summary: Matt Rice detailed Alternative C3.4, a wider four-story option focusing on pool and gymnasium preservation with additions built over existing practice fields.

items.title: Alternative D1.1: Six-Story New Construction on Parking Lot
items.summary: Matt Rice described Alternative D1.1, a new six-story facility built on the existing parking lot that requires 76 modular classrooms due to footprints overlapping with the existing building.

items.title: Alternative D2.1: New Construction on Edgerly Field
items.summary: Matt Rice presented Alternative D2.1, which builds a new school on Edgerly Field and eliminates the need for modular classrooms by keeping the old facility operational during construction.

items.title: Community Q&A Session
items.summary: Panelists answered public questions regarding modular classrooms, high-rise building code cost premiums, and the potential relocation of community programs and the Curtis-Tufts school.

items.title: Upcoming Meetings and Next Steps
items.summary: Matt Gulino outlined the schedule of upcoming building committee meetings, community forums, and public outreach events planned through June.
